title: Polynomial parameters and their global multiplication kernels
statement: Let k:Type u be a field, Lambda:Type w a Noetherian geometrically regular k-algebra, and q a prime of Lambda. Put L=Lambda_q and d=spanFinrank(m_L). Let e>0. Fix a polynomial k-algebra P=k[y:Fin m0], a map phi0:P to Lambda, p0=phi0 inverse image of q, and a flat local localization map psi0:P_(p0) to L commuting with phi0, such that p0 extends to m_L. There exist uP:Fin d to P in p0, generating p0 P_(p0), whose images form a regular sequence in L, such that for gamma_i=C(uP_i)t_i in T=P[t:Fin d], multiplication by gamma_i and gamma_i squared have equal kernels on T/(gamma_j^e:j<i). The exact rings, maps and equalities are in the attached Lean signature. The notions are those of the statement-dependency nodes.

proof.text: Geometric regularity applied to a universe-lift of the trivial field extension makes Lambda regular, by tensor-product equivalences. The Mathlib polynomial regular-ring instance makes P regular. The commuting square and maximal-ideal extension equality show that psi maps the source maximal ideal onto the target maximal ideal, hence is local. Apply the flat height formula at these maximal ideals; the image maximal ideal in the closed-fibre quotient is zero, so its height is zero. Regularity of L identifies its Krull dimension with its maximal-ideal generator rank d, giving dimension d also for P_p.

Choose a finite generating set of the source maximal ideal of cardinality its spanFinrank=d, enumerate it by Fin d, and express each generator as a fraction f_i/t_i. The numerator f_i lies in p by the maximal-ideal criterion for fractions. Since each denominator maps to a unit, the numerator images have the same ideal span. These d generators are a regular system of parameters; the regular-local generators theorem gives regularity of every permutation.

Apply the proved coefficient-kernel-rescaling theorem to f, p, d and e. It supplies factors s_i outside p and all polynomial kernel equalities for uP_i=s_i f_i. Membership in p follows because p is an ideal. Unit images of s_i preserve the source maximal-ideal span, by span_range_mul_units.

Map the source span equality along psi, using Ideal.map_span and Ideal.map_map and the commuting square. The given maximal-ideal equality identifies the result with the target maximal ideal. The images of uP therefore form a length-d regular system of parameters in the regular local ring L. Apply the regular-local generators theorem to obtain their regularity, and combine it with membership, the source span and the kernel equalities. All constructions and inductions also handle d=0.

proof_origin.place: Lemma Tag 07FJ (lemma-resolve-general), item-choose-pii and item-modify-pii; polynomial regularity is the direct Mathlib instance for Stacks 00OQ

mathlib_searches.query: choose regular local parameters from a flat polynomial chart and rescale to equalize multiplication kernels

mathlib_searches.results: RegularLocalRing.Defs has dimension and generator-rank identities, but no combined selection and Ogoma rescaling theorem. No Ogoma result in Mathlib.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_popescu_polynomial_kernel_parameters
    {k : Type u} {Λ : Type w}
    [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum Λ) (hreg : IsGeometricallyRegular k Λ)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : d =
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)).spanFinrank)
    (e : ℕ) (he : 0 < e)
    (m₀ : ℕ) (φ₀ : MvPolynomial (Fin m₀) k →ₐ[k] Λ)
    (ψ₀ : Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.comap φ₀.toRingHom) →+*
      Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
    (hψ₀ : ψ₀.comp (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m₀) k)
        (Localization.AtPrime (q.asIdeal.comap φ₀.toRingHom))) =
      (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)).comp φ₀.toRingHom)
    (hideal₀ : q.asIdeal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)) =
      (q.asIdeal.comap φ₀.toRingHom).map
        ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)).comp φ₀.toRingHom))
    (hflat₀ : ψ₀.Flat) :
    let P := MvPolynomial (Fin m₀) k
    let p₀ := q.asIdeal.comap φ₀.toRingHom
    let L := Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal
    ∃ uP : Fin d → P,
      (∀ i, uP i ∈ p₀) ∧
      Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ algebraMap P (Localization.AtPrime p₀) (uP i))) =
        p₀.map (algebraMap P (Localization.AtPrime p₀)) ∧
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular L
        (List.ofFn (fun i ↦ algebraMap Λ L (φ₀ (uP i)))) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin d)
        (x : MvPolynomial (Fin d) P ⧸ Ideal.span
          {y | ∃ j : Fin d, j.val < i.val ∧
            y = (MvPolynomial.C (uP j) * MvPolynomial.X j) ^ e}),
        (MvPolynomial.C (uP i) * MvPolynomial.X i) • x = 0 ↔
          (MvPolynomial.C (uP i) * MvPolynomial.X i) ^ 2 • x = 0)
